_why: THIRD held-out batch. Never used to choose or tune a change.
Written for M21, before any code for it existed and before any run of
these cases. M21 makes the system connect a claim shared with another
insurance policy to the policy's contribution clause (6.6), because the
main-set case `other-policy-contribution` never cited 6.6. A fix designed
around one case is a fix tuned to that case, so these test the same idea
in words that case does not use, plus one situation that mentions another
insurer and must NOT bring in the contribution clause.
Same synthetic policy and conventions as scenarios.json. Same author as
the fix, so not fully independent - but fixed before the fix was built.

cases.scenario: My employer's group health insurance paid part of my hospital bill for a three-day stay with typhoid, and I am claiming the rest under this policy, which I have held for three years. I am 41.
cases.why: A second policy covers the same stay, so this insurer pays no more than its rateable proportion. The stay itself is payable: three years clears the 30-day initial wait, and typhoid is in no waiting-period list.

cases.scenario: I have two health insurance policies, this one and a family floater from another company. I had my appendix removed and spent five days in hospital, and I am claiming on both. I have held this policy two years and I am 38.
cases.why: Two policies covering one claim is exactly the contribution clause: paid, but only this insurer's rateable share.

cases.scenario: Last year I left my old insurer and bought this policy instead, and I no longer have the old one. I was in hospital for four days with dengue fever last month. I am 35.
cases.why: The contribution clause applies only to another policy held at the time of the claim, and the old one has lapsed. One year held clears the 30-day initial wait, dengue is in no waiting-period list, and nothing reduces an ordinary in-patient stay for a 35-year-old.
